extracted.intended_audience: members of the District of Columbia Bar (D.C. attorneys), Bar administrators, and applicants to the D.C. Bar
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural requirements promulgated by the District of Columbia Court of Appeals governing the organization, membership, officers, governance, meetings, finances, and related administrative procedures of the District of Columbia Bar; includes related appellate appendix and fee-waiver criteria excerpted in the file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naming respondents in OAH cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed amendment to R.15 to make clear that the Office of Administrative Hearings (OAH) should not be named as a respondent; incorporate statutory language: 'Only the parties before [OAH] or any other party permitted to participate by the reviewing court shall be parties in any such proceeding for judicial review.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The court concluded any ambiguity in 'parties before [OAH]' is best addressed through litigation rather than rulemaking and adopted the proposed amendments as sent out for comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date of rule amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: These amendments will go into effect sixty days from the date of this order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clean and track-changes versions of the rules as amended are attached to the order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purposes of the Bar
rubrics_metrics.description: The purposes of the Bar shall be (a) to assist the legal profession in maintaining high standards of the practice of law in the District of Columbia; (b) to aid the courts of the District of Columbia in carrying out and improving the administration of justice; (c) to promote access to justice and enhance the delivery of legal services to those in need; (d) to foster and maintain on the part of those engaged in the practice of law high ideals of integrity, learning, competence in public service, and high ethical standards; (e) to safeguard the proper professional interests of the members of the Bar; (f) to encourage the formation and support the activities of volunteer bar associations; (g) to provide a forum for and publish information about the practice of law, the science of jurisprudence and law reform, and the relationship of the Bar to the public; and (h) to carry on a continuing program of legal research and education in the technical fields of substantive law, practice and procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These enumerated purposes define the core mission and permissible activities of the District of Columbia Bar as an official arm of the Court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: All persons admitted to practice law in the District of Columbia are organized as members of the District of Columbia Bar and are subject to the provisions of these Rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Residence in the District of Columbia shall not be a condition of eligibility to membership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory course for new admittees
rubrics_metrics.description: The Bar shall establish and administer a course on the District of Columbia Rules of Professional Conduct and on District of Columbia practice; within twelve months after admission to the Bar all members shall complete such course and certify compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to complete the course or otherwise satisfy related requirements may result in suspension from the Bar and inability to practice; the Bar shall report annually to the Court addressing curriculum, faculty, number of presentations, attendance, and number suspended for noncompliance. In tracked-change text: the course must be presented at least six times per year; noncompliance triggers written notice and suspension if not corrected within sixty days; reinstatement upon completion and fulfilling administrative requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classes of membership
rubrics_metrics.description: Members shall be divided into classes (active, judicial, inactive, retired); inactive members are eligible for active membership but not engaged in practice and must request enrollment; judicial members include judges and persons performing judicial function on an exclusive basis; retired members are those who have retired or are totally disabled and meet service/practice-year requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retired members must certify (a) five years as an active member (two years of any combination of inactive or judicial may substitute for one year of active), and (b) 25 years engaged in the practice of law. Except as provided in Rule 49(c), judicial, inactive, or retired members are not entitled to practice law in D.C., hold office, vote in general elections, or vote on Bar business. The Board may create additional classes after consultation with the Court.

rubrics_metrics.name: License fees and dues ceiling
rubrics_metrics.description: The District of Columbia Court of Appeals shall set a ceiling for annual license fees (dues); the Board of Governors shall determine the amount to be paid by members in the classes of membership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All fees are paid to the Bar and constitute a fund for expenses. The Board may recommend changes to the ceiling; recommendations must be published and members have 60 days to comment. Recommendations for increases in the ceiling are not subject to referendum under Rule VII. Non-payment of license fees may result in suspension and inability to practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resignation and reinstatement procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: A member’s resignation from and reinstatement into the Bar shall be governed by procedures prescribed by the Bar and shall include consultation with the Office of Disciplinary Counsel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinstatement following suspension or assumption of inactive status or resignation is governed by rules promulgated by the Board of Governors after consultation with the Board on Professional Responsibility; in appropriate cases the Board may reinstate nunc pro tunc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secretary's duty to notify the Court Clerk
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary of the Bar shall forward forthwith to the Clerk of the Court the names of those attorneys who have registered with the Bar and those whose membership status has been changed in any way pursuant to the provisions of this Rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures the Court's roll is updated promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Officers: composition, eligibility, and term
rubrics_metrics.description: The officers of the Bar shall be a President, a President-Elect, a Secretary, and a Treasurer; only active members are eligible to serve; the term of each officer is one year; officers receive no compensation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Duties of officers and process for filling vacancies are set forth in the Bylaws. Officers may be nominated and either elected or appointed per the Bylaws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board of Governors composition and authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The affairs of the Bar shall be managed by a Board of Governors consisting of the officers, the Immediate Past-President, and fifteen members elected by the Bar; the Treasurer-Elect shall be among the fifteen elected non-officer members; the Board may appoint non-voting members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board has general charge of the affairs and activities of the Bar in accordance with the Rules and Bylaws, including making appropriations, engaging employees, receiving and acting on committee reports, arranging publication of official bulletins, conducting investigations, filling vacancies, and adopting Bylaws and regulations not inconsistent with the Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public statements by the Bar
rubrics_metrics.description: No opinion of the Bar on any matter involving legislation of major public interest or concern or of major importance to the members of the Bar shall be publicly expressed unless authorized by the Board of Governors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rule limits public advocacy to positions authorized by the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meetings of the Bar (annual and special)
rubrics_metrics.description: There shall be an annual meeting of members of the Bar; special meetings may be called in a manner set forth in the Bylaws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board of Governors determines time/place for the annual meeting and arranges a suitable program. Special meetings may be called by Board, President, or the Secretary upon petition of at least 3% of active members (see referendum/meeting procedures).

rubrics_metrics.name: Referendum procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board of Governors may refer any question of Bar policy to active members by ballot with a 2/3 affirmative vote; members may initiate a referendum by petition signed by not less than 3% of active members based on the census as of the first business day of the calendar year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ballots shall be prepared, distributed, returned and counted per regulations prescribed by the Board; a majority of votes cast controls the action of the Bar and its organs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disbursements and financial reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board shall make necessary appropriations for disbursements from Bar funds to pay necessary expenses and shall keep proper books and procure an annual audit by a certified public accountant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At each annual meeting the Board shall present a financial statement showing assets, liabilities, receipts, and disbursements; a copy shall be transmitted to the Clerk of the Court and published in an official Bar publication prior to the annual meeting, accompanied by a detailed statement reflecting all significant components of total disbursements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adoption of Bylaws
rubrics_metrics.description: Bylaws not inconsistent with the Rules may be established by a majority vote of the voting members of the Board of Governors at a meeting with at least two-thirds of the voting Board members in attendance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bylaws must conform to the Rules; the Board may adopt regulations for orderly administration not inconsistent with these Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodic registration of attorneys
rubrics_metrics.description: Every attorney who engages in the practice of law within the District of Columbia shall on or before July 1 of every year file with the Secretary of the Bar a registration statement setting forth residence and office addresses, email, telephone, other state jurisdictions and date of admission, and other information as the Court may direct; supplemental statements must be filed within thirty days of change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An attorney who becomes newly subject shall file within three months or by the following July 1. Failure to file after due notice may result in summary suspension from membership by the Board and bar from practice until reinstated. Attorneys who retire or are not engaged in practice must advise the Secretary in writing/electronically to assume inactive status and must file registration statements for 5 years thereafter for location in case of complaints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory course: presentation frequency and enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: The mandatory course on the Rules of Professional Conduct and D.C. practice must be presented at least six times per year; members admitted after July 1, 1994 must complete within twelve months and certify compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bar will give written notice of noncompliance; failure to comply within sixty days of notice results in suspension from membership. Reinstatement follows completion of the course and fulfillment of any administrative requirements imposed by the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and eligibility rules for retired, judicial, and inactive members
rubrics_metrics.description: Judges of courts of record, full-time commissioners, bankruptcy and magistrate judges, and others performing judicial functions exclusively shall be judicial members; inactive members are eligible but not engaged in practice and have requested inactive status; retired members are those retired from practice or totally disabled and who satisfy years-of-service and practice requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inactive and judicial members no longer eligible to practice unless they request and are granted transfer to active class and pay required license fees; retired members must meet specified active-membership and practice-year thresholds; limitations on holding office, voting, and practicing are specified and cross-referenced to Rule 49.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalties for nonpayment of dues and late charges
rubrics_metrics.description: If annual dues/license fees remain unpaid at expiration of 90 days from due date, membership may be suspended by the Board in the manner provided in the Bylaws; the Board may impose a reasonable late charge to offset notification costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No person whose membership is suspended for nonpayment shall be entitled to practice law in D.C. during the suspension period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Officer vacancy and succession rules
rubrics_metrics.description: If the President dies, is permanently disabled, or resigns before term expiration, the President-Elect has the option to succeed to the office and serve the remainder of the term and subsequently the elected presidential term; if the President-Elect declines, the Board shall elect a member to serve the remainder of the term and that person shall serve as past president the following year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similar procedures govern vacancies in the office of President-Elect, including election of a Vice President and special elections when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegation of officers' duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Any duties imposed on the Secretary or Treasurer by the Rules or Bylaws may be performed under their supervision by assistants or employees of the Bar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delegation must be under supervision of the named officer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Committee composition and limits on authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Executive Committee consists of the President, President-Elect, Immediate Past-President, and 4 additional members selected annually by the Board; five members constitute a quorum; action by a majority of members present constitutes committee action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Executive Committee may exercise Board powers between meetings except it shall not, unless authorized by the Board, (a) amend the Bylaws, (b) make rules or regulations governing nominations or elections, or (c) initiate any referendum or poll of Bar members. The President presides and the Secretary keeps minutes which must be distributed to the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meetings: quorum, attendance, notice, and member recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: One hundred active members present at any annual or special meeting shall constitute a quorum; members cannot be represented by proxy; 'present' includes in person or virtual/electronic attendance so long as all attendees can hear each other and participate meaningfully.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice of annual meeting must be mailed or published at least 30 days prior; notice of special meetings at least 10 days prior. Members present may adopt proposals by vote which become recommendations to the Board, subject to Bylaws limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix requirements for appeals (briefing/appendix production)
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendix materials shall follow the table of contents and other parts of the record chronologically; when transcript pages are included, the date and page numbers must be listed on a separate page immediately before included pages; omissions must be indicated by asterisks; immaterial formal matters should be omitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exhibits designated for inclusion may be reproduced in a separate indexed volume; four copies must be filed with each copy of the appendix and one copy served on counsel for each separately represented party. For good cause, court may permit appeal on the original record without an appendix. In fee-waiver or CJA cases no appendix is required but the appellant must file four copies of any opinion, findings of fact, and conclusions of law that relate to issues raised; appellee may file four copies of additional portions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of court fees and costs (D.C. Code § 15–712 criteria and process)
rubrics_metrics.description: In any noncriminal suit, the court shall grant a full waiver of fees/costs/security if the litigant submits an application with a declaration showing (A) the litigant or dependent receives financial assistance from listed District programs, (B) receives assistance from listed federal programs, (C) monthly income does not exceed 200% of federal poverty guidelines, or (D) is represented free by a legal services or qualifying law clinic. The court may grant full or partial waivers for other litigants who show inability to proceed without substantial hardship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court may require additional evidence, delegate waiver authority to clerk (denials/partial grants by judge), decide within 5 calendar days (or grant full waiver if not ruled), provide hearings on denial within 14 days, maintain financial application confidentiality with limited exceptions, not consider the merit of the underlying suit when deciding waiver, not impose fees for filing waiver applications or related papers (subject to stated exceptions), attempt service of complaints for waived cases, allow motions for free transcripts (granted unless frivolous and may be limited to necessary documents).
